key_insight: An uncertainty-aware framework translates predicted patient deterioration risk into ICU staffing plans that balance cost and exposure to severe shortages.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support ICU workforce planning while accounting for rigid shifts and hiring delays, without changing the underlying prediction model.
method: Aggregate patient risk predictions while explicitly modeling changing predictive uncertainty.
Use Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) to assess extreme staffing-shortage exposure.
Generate delay-constrained staffing decisions through hourly rolling-horizon scheduling.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on realistic MIMIC-IV trajectories showed a favorable cost–shortage trade-off versus deterministic and reactive baselines, with robustness assessed under simulated calibration drift.
watch_item: Trajectory-based evaluation does not establish real-world staffing benefits or patient safety; prospective validation is needed.
paper_title: From Clinical Risk Prediction to Operational Decisions: An Uncertainty-Aware Framework for ICU Staffing
